newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy unions ask to see PM over metalworkers row.
newsitem.headline: Italy unions ask to see PM over metalworkers row.

text.p: Italian unions want to meet Prime Minister Romano Prodi and employers' organisation Confindustria to discuss wage issues in the light of the long-running metalworkers' dispute, union leader Sergio D'Antoni said.
Earlier on Monday leaders of the three big union federations, Cigl, Cisl and Uil, held talks with bosses from the three metalworkers' unions, the Fim, Fiom and Uilm.

"Our evaluation of the dispute today is not positive. It is necessary to meet Prodi so that the government clears up its position," D'Antoni, the leader of the Cisl union, told reporters at a press conference.
The general secretary of Cgil, Sergio Coferati, said Confindustria should also be present at the meeting.
"There is a binding need for a meeting of clarification with the government and Confindustria on incomes policy," he said.

Michele Figurati, the leader of the federation of metalworkers employers Federmeccanica, met the leader of the Fiom union on Monday. "The details of the meeting are absolutely private," Fiom's Claudio Sabattini said.
The metalworkers' dispute has been dragging on since last June, with unions and management unable to agree on pay awards for the 1996/98 contractural period.
In a bid to break the deadlock, the centre-left government suggested last month that workers should receive an average monthly pay rise of 200,000 lire ($127).
Unions, who had been seeking 230,000 lire, agreed, but management have stuck to their 139,000 lire offer.
Federmeccanica has been seeking tax breaks from the government and lower-cost contracts for workers in the underdeveloped south of the country.
Employers' chiefs expressed cautious optimism last week that a solution might soon be found to the dispute. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501 ($ = 1574 Italian Lire)
